brief: The bead-spirit unwinding a long string of twenty-two glass beads across a mossy root, each bead catching the firelight, a different colour; Dādī leaning in to count them; Śuka pecking at the beads gently.

The burning-ground grove at night: the Vetāla seated on a root rubbing his hands; a tiny round spirit of old paper in round spectacles with scrolls under both arms and one finger wagging at the sky; Dādī and Śuka beside you; a faint image in the smoke of a king and a hungry beggar on a lane.

The burning-ground grove at night: a small spirit shaped like a rolled-up storybook with stubby legs and a bright storyteller's turban drumming on its own spine with two fingers; the Vetāla seated on a root in a dramatic storytelling pose; you, Dādī and Śuka around a small fire.

The Vetāla seated near a small fire telling a tale with a raised finger; the storybook spirit beating a drum-roll on his spine; Lubdhaka stopping at the edge of the firelight, pulled in by the drum; you, Dādī and Śuka around the fire.

A very small quick hand reaching out of an open drawer in the little spirit's body and snatching a pencil from behind his ear; the spirit squealing; the Vetāla amused; Dādī and Śuka laughing; firelight.

A tiny figure of mist spilling out of an opened drawer in the little spirit's body, turning on one foot with arms wide in a dance; the drawer-spirit staring at it in wonder; the Vetāla smiling; Dādī pointing; lamplight.
The ledger-spirit opening a small drawer with two fingers and lifting out a tiny silver needle; the Vetāla and Dādī leaning in to look; a pinprick of light at the needle's tip; firelight.

A small plain ash-coloured spirit stepping out of an opened drawer, without any marks or ornaments, patting itself to check it is there; Dhātuka holding his ledger a little pale; the Vetāla and Dādī watching; firelight.
